title: OpenAI Reportedly Raises $11 Billion at $1.25 Trillion Valuation, Short of Its Target
excerpt: Bloomberg reported $11 billion raised so far in a round that has not closed and could total about $20 billion, well below the $30 billion OpenAI was reported to be seeking in September.
body:
• OpenAI has reportedly raised $11 billion so far in a new funding round that values the company at $1.25 trillion, Bloomberg reported on Friday, citing sources familiar with the matter.
  • The $11 billion is only part of a larger round that has not closed yet; the round is expected to close in the coming weeks and could total about $20 billion, a source told Bloomberg.
  • That target is well short of the $30 billion OpenAI was reported to be seeking in late September, and earlier reporting put the valuation it hoped for at $1.4 trillion.
  • OpenAI has not publicly confirmed the figures: TechCrunch said it had reached out to the company for comment, and the reported numbers rest on anonymous sources, not a company announcement.

OpenAI has reportedly raised $11 billion so far in a new funding round valuing the artificial intelligence company at $1.25 trillion, TechCrunch reported, citing Bloomberg's reporting on Friday from sources familiar with the matter. Reuters, in separate reporting carried by Unite.AI, described the $11 billion as an initial close within a larger financing and said SoftBank and MGX participated, according to two investors.

Reported versus sought

The distinction between what was sought and what has been committed is the core of the story. In late September, Bloomberg reported that OpenAI was looking to raise $30 billion in the upcoming round. The current figures fall well short of that target, TechCrunch said. Reporting in late October told the same story in stages: about $11 billion had been committed by an October 31 deadline, less than half the original $30 billion ask, The Wall Street Journal reported, and the Financial Times said the target had since been cut to about $20 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation, down from $30 billion at $1.4 trillion, after several investors reduced their allocations, The Inference summarised. Those are reported targets and commitments, not company-disclosed results, and the final total can still change because the round has not closed.

Where the figures come from

None of the numbers in this round comes from OpenAI itself. Bloomberg's account rests on sources familiar with the matter, and TechCrunch said it had reached out to OpenAI for comment and would update if the company responded. Readers should therefore treat the $11 billion, the roughly $20 billion expected total and the $1.25 trillion valuation as reported figures attributed to anonymous sources, not as confirmed company disclosures. The last round OpenAI did announce itself was different in kind: in its funding announcement, the company said it had closed a round with $122 billion in committed capital at a post-money valuation of $852 billion, anchored by Amazon, NVIDIA and SoftBank, with continued participation from Microsoft. Against that confirmed baseline, a $1.25 trillion mark would be a step up in valuation even as the new round's size comes in below its original ambition.

Why investors are marking AI down

The trimmed round landed in a cooler market for artificial intelligence valuations. TechCrunch noted the news came only hours after Bloomberg also reported that potential buyers of shares in the initial public offering of OpenAI's chief competitor, Anthropic, were eyeing a substantially lower valuation than Anthropic had targeted: some potential buyers believed Anthropic's valuation could be as low as $1.1 trillion, compared with the $2 trillion investors were said to be expecting roughly a month earlier. TechCrunch also reported that the Democratic landslide in the US midterms and negative voter sentiment around data centers had caused jitters throughout the market, with many anticipating potential regulatory challenges. That context matters for how the shortfall is read: it reflects pricing and timing in a repricing sector, not a disclosed change in OpenAI's own reported business.

What to watch next

Two things will settle the story. The first is the closing itself: Bloomberg's source expected the round to close in the coming weeks at about $20 billion, and any company confirmation, final total or named investor list would replace the current anonymous-source reporting. The second is OpenAI's path to public markets. The company previously indicated it would go public this year but subsequently delayed its plans, and there are expectations it will hold its initial public offering next year at some point, TechCrunch reported. A private round priced at $1.25 trillion, below the valuation the company was reported to have hoped for, will be the benchmark investors carry into that listing debate. For Indian and diaspora engineers, founders and investors who work in and around the US AI industry, the practical read is narrower: frontier AI capital is still available in very large amounts, but the price and size of that capital are now being negotiated down in public view.
